test_contract:
Three observable contracts, one of them the deciding row.

(1) EXTERNAL STREAM MONOTONICITY (packages/tui/test/tool-execution-xdev-render.test.ts). Stream a `write` whose path is `xd://probe` in increasing argument prefixes through a real `ToolExecutionComponent`; the mounted `probeTool.renderCall` records the `options.rawArgs.json` it is handed. Contract: the recorded strings are monotonically non-decreasing in length, each is a prefix of the next, and the last one is the OUTER write-call buffer (it contains `"path":"xd://probe"`), NOT the inner device payload (which contains `"command"`). Consumer-observable failure: a `xd://` device card whose raw preview freezes at the first parsed checkpoint, or — the bug this item exists to prevent — shows the inner device JSON while the outer stream is still growing, so the card misrepresents how much of the call has arrived.

(2) REBUILD/LIVE PARITY (same file). Drive the same tool call twice — once through the live reveal path, once through the ui-helpers.ts:605 rebuild path — and assert both produce byte-identical final render. Consumer-observable failure: a card changes appearance when the user changes theme, toggles a setting, or refocuses mid-stream. This defends the third path the plan mislocated; note the plan's stated file (chat-transcript-builder.ts) is the wrong file entirely and would leave this contract undefended.

(3) THE ADAPTER REACH CONTRACT (packages/coding-agent/test/extensions/raw-args-render-channel.test.ts) — the deciding row. A tool registered through `registerTool({ renderResult })`, wrapped by `RegisteredToolAdapter` (and separately by `customToolToDefinition`), receives `rawArgs`, `argsComplete` and `executionStarted` on its options. Consumer-observable failure: an out-of-repo extension that gates its streaming preview on `options.argsComplete` renders as though nothing ever completed, forever, because the field is declared in the type and thrown away at the adapter. This test is green on a fix that only adds the field to the interface, and green on the built-in `xd://` path alone — that is precisely what makes it the deciding row, and it is the one thing `bun run check:ts` provably cannot catch.

Negative assertion required in (3): an option field that was never present must not appear, so the adapter fix cannot regress into an untyped blanket passthrough that would also leak internal render bookkeeping to extensions.

Not a contract, do not test: that the interface has N members; that `rawArgs` exists; that the code 'ran'.

test_contract:
Defends three named contracts.

(1) LOST-UPDATE ELIMINATION. Observable contract: after two independent PluginManager instances (each holding its OWN memoized config, both pointed at the same lockfile) run setEnabled concurrently, the JSON on disk contains BOTH changes. If it regresses, the user sees a plugin toggle silently vanish because another writer touched the lockfile first — the exact failure that motivated M4-4.

    Test geometry is load-bearing and the plan is right about it. `#ensureConfigLoaded` (manager.ts:141-146) memoizes `this.#runtimeConfig` per instance, so two setEnabled calls on ONE instance mutate one shared object and the second write necessarily contains both changes EVEN WITH THE LOCK ENTIRELY REMOVED. A single-instance test is therefore green on the unfixed code and defends nothing. The test must construct two PluginManager instances and assert each loads its own config. Note that `getPluginsLockfile` is a GLOBAL path (~/.omp/plugins/omp-plugins.lock.json via dirs.ts:652), NOT cwd-derived, so both instances must be pointed at one temp lockfile via the spyOn pattern.

(2) THE NEGATIVE CONTROL — mandatory, without it (1) proves nothing. Re-run scenario (1) against the PRE-fix algorithm, written out inline in the test as a plain mutate-then-Bun.write helper with no lock, and assert the disk file contains only ONE of the two changes. This is the row that makes (1) meaningful: it demonstrates the failure the lock removes, using the real file, the real path, and the real algorithm.

    Implementation constraint: drive this with an inline re-implementation, NOT by patching PluginManager. AGENTS.md bans `mock.module()` outright, and patching the class to remove its own lock would be the same kind of lie. The inline helper writes the same bytes to the same spied lockfile — that is a real reproduction, not a mock.

(3) ChangeResult SEMANTICS, one test per branch:
    - setEnabled to the value it already holds returns changed:false and leaves the file bytes untouched. (Distinct outcome from the success path — this is the branch that proves `changed` is observed on disk rather than echoing a returned flag.)
    - deletePluginSetting on an absent key returns changed:false.
    - setEnabled on an unknown plugin still rejects with /not found in runtime config/ AND leaves the file untouched — proving the throw happens inside the lock before any write, so a failed call cannot corrupt the lockfile.
    - setEnabled returns application: 'restart-required' (the no-HMR path).

Also assert, for the extracted helper: atomicWriteJson leaves no `.tmp` sibling behind and produces parseable JSON with the trailing newline. The Windows EPERM fallback is NOT testable on darwin-arm64 — do not fake it with a source grep or a forced errno; state it as untested here.

Full-suite safety: use the exact isolation pattern from packages/coding-agent/test/plugin-config.test.ts:19-33 — `spyOn(piUtils, 'getPluginsDir'|'getPluginsLockfile'|'getProjectDir'|'getProjectPluginOverridesPath')` in beforeEach, `mock.restore()` in afterEach, `fs.mkdtemp` under `os.tmpdir()` and `removeWithRetries` for cleanup. No file-wide mutation of `Bun.*` or `process.env`.

AGENTS.md compliance: every test here names a consumer-observable failure mode. Do not add a test that only asserts the constructor or the file exists. Do NOT source-grep manager.ts or registry.ts to prove the refactor happened — the `git grep saveRuntimeConfig` check in step 5 is a human checklist item, not a test.

Under option (a) there is a second, deliberate contract: a shadowed row reports `shadowedBy === undefined`, which pins the current gap so a later refactor that starts populating it knows to revisit this test instead of silently changing what the CLI claims. Under option (b) that same assertion inverts into the regression test for the fix: a shadowed row MUST name its shadow source, and if a refactor reintroduces a bare `item._shadowed = true` the test goes red instead of the field quietly going back to undefined.
